items.title: Pay for 'Branchenregister' entry
items.quote: Der Betrag von 569,06 € ist bis zum 16.09.2027 zu überweisen.
items.computation: The letter states an explicit calendar date for payment: 16.09.2027. This is a Thursday (letter dated Thursday 09.09.2027, today 11.09.2027 is a Saturday, so 16.09.2027 falls 5 days later = Thursday), which is a normal business day in NW with no public holiday, so no weekend/holiday shift under §193 BGB is needed. Note: the underlying claim is highly doubtful (see warnings) — this appears to be an unsolicited 'Branchenbuch' offer dressed up as an invoice, so there may be no real obligation to pay at all.

warnings: This matches the well-known German 'Branchenbuch'/'Verzeichnisservice' scam pattern: an unsolicited-looking 'Eintragungsbestätigung und Rechnung' that is legally only an offer, not a confirmed order — the letter itself admits this ('Die Eintragung ist ein Angebot; mit Ihrer Zahlung nehmen Sie es an.'), meaning paying is what creates a contract, not fulfilling one you already agreed to.

The payee name on the IBAN ('BRM Verlagsservice Ltd.') does not match the sender name on the letterhead ('Branchenregister Musterland – Verzeichnisservice'), which is a common red flag for this type of scam.

The threat to hand the matter straight to a debt-collection agency 'ohne weitere Mahnung' (without a further reminder) after a very short 7-day deadline is a pressure tactic typical of these fake directory invoices.

There is no indication the recipient actually requested or ordered this business-directory entry; before paying, verify whether any order was actually placed and consider consulting consumer protection (Verbraucherzentrale) — such invoices are frequently reported as scams and are often not legally owed.

No legal-remedy instructions (Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung) are present because this is a private commercial letter, not an administrative decision; declining to pay an unsolicited offer generally does not require any formal objection.
